# package ieee2030

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-otfp/protocols/ieee2030"
```

Package ieee2030 fingerprints IEEE 2030.5 (Smart Energy Profile 2.0), the HTTPS/REST protocol between a utility server and distributed energy resources.

IEEE 2030.5 mandates mutual TLS with the cipher suite TLS\_ECDHE\_ECDSA\_WITH\_AES\_128\_CCM\_8 and ECDSA certificates. Without a device certificate a probe cannot read the data model, so detection examines the TLS layer: the fingerprinter completes a handshake far enough to see whether the server requests a client certificate and presents an ECDSA server certificate — the shape of an IEEE 2030.5 server — then, if the handshake can be finished (an anonymous or misconfigured server), reads GET /dcap and recognises the DeviceCapability document and the urn:ieee:std:2030.5:ns namespace, which is conclusive.

The probe reads the TLS layer directly: it sends its own TLS 1.2 ClientHello offering CCM\_8 (and common ECDHE suites) and parses the server's plaintext flight — the cipher suite chosen, the certificate's key type, and whether a client certificate is requested — without completing a handshake. A server choosing CCM\_8, the IEEE 2030.5 suite that the Go standard library does not implement (GridAPPS-D offers only it), is recognised even though no Go TLS client could talk to it.
